correctness.rationale: For product weights on disjoint coordinate blocks, the rectangular A2 characteristic factors exactly; for tensor-product test functions, the strong maximal operator and weighted L2 norm ratios factor exactly. Tensoring floor(d/2) copies of Lerner's two-dimensional A sqrt(log A) obstruction yields characteristic comparable to theta^{-floor(d/2)} and norm at least theta^{-floor(d/2)}(log(1/theta))^{floor(d/2)/2}, which converts to the stated A(log A)^{floor(d/2)/2} lower family. An extra unweighted coordinate handles odd dimensions without reducing the norm ratio.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Lerner's September 2026 result states the logarithmic obstruction in dimension two, while Ombrosi--Rey give all-dimensional upper bounds. Searches for higher-dimensional tensor/product-weight and logarithmic strong-maximal lower bounds found no prior statement of the amplified A(log A)^{floor(d/2)/2} family or the corresponding necessary logarithmic exponent.

value.rationale: The result upgrades the newly discovered two-dimensional failure of a linear rectangular-A2 bound into a dimension-growing hierarchy: every disjoint coordinate pair forces an additional square-root logarithm, ruling out all near-linear logarithmic exponents below floor(d/2)/2.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, formal verification, or a guarantee of first discovery.
